messages:
rachel: Heads up — runtime change merged for 429 handling. SDKs now prefer soft-fallbacks + context trimming by default. We need a tiny migration note and a couple of quick examples (Node + Python) in the Troubleshooting / 429 section. Who can take?

alex: I can do the Node snippet. what phrasing do we want for the behavior? short and prescriptive.

linh: I'm happy to do the python snippet and a short paragraph explaining why the new fallback is safer (avoids head-of-line blocking + keeps latency SLOs).

kevin: FYI product wants the wording to call out: when app-level ordering matters, pin to "no-fallback" policy. Otherwise recommend accepting fallback for degraded quality.

rachel: yes call that out. also add an example of checking for 429 vs other transient errors. Keep it < 6 lines each.

alex: Draft Node sample: ```js
// Node SDK: prefer soft fallback + exponential jitter
const res = await client.generate({ prompt }, {
  maxRetries: 3,
  backoff: { type: 'exponential', baseMs: 100, jitter: true },
  fallbackStrategy: 'soft' // returns best-effort shorter completion on 429
});
```

linh: Draft Python sample: ```py
# Python SDK: explicit check + context trim helper
from redwood import Client, trim_context
client = Client()
ctx = trim_context(history, max_tokens=1500)
try:
    out = client.generate(prompt=ctx, max_retries=3, backoff='exp_jitter')
except ClientError as e:
    if e.code == 429:
        # fallback: call with shorter context or retry with backoff
        out = client.generate(prompt=trim_context(ctx, 800), fallback=True)
    else:
        raise
```

rachel: Nice. Can we add one-liner guidance above each: "When to use fallback" and "When to pin to no-fallback"?

kevin: +1. Also request a short note pointing to Dedicated customers who can request reserved capacity instead of relying on fallbacks.

alex: I'll open a PR with Node snippet and the short guidance. PR title: "docs(429): quick migration note + Node snippet for soft fallback". tagging @linh for python example.

linh: I'll add the python snippet in a follow-up commit in the same PR.

docs-bot: New draft PR created by alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/812 — rachel, linch pinned. :eyes:

rachel: thanks. small editorial asks before merge: avoid the phrase "best-effort" (legal prefers "degraded-quality fallback"), and include a one-line compatibility note about older SDKs not supporting fallbackStrategy.

alex: will update wording. also add a tiny table row in the error-ref listing: 429 -> fallbackStrategy, context-trim recommendation, when to pin.

kevin: remember to include a quick test plan in the PR description: steps to repro (synthetic 429), verify fallback returns shorter output and logs event `fallback.used`.

rachel: Perfect. Let's aim to merge today. If anyone runs into wording pushback I'll loop in legal. :shipit:

linh: I'll check the PR this afternoon and add python + one-liner guidance.

alex: PR updated with wording, test plan, and short Node snippet. pinging for review.

rachel: Reviewed and left minor nits. Once fixed, merge. Thanks all. :tada:
